content.summary: In this mission, you will read an article about how modern workers handle stress and protect their wellbeing. You will learn to spot key phrasal verbs, identify cause-and-effect relationships, and scan for practical lifestyle advice.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Multi-word verbs with specific particles: burn out, wind down, cope with, cut back on, take up, and reach out.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Terms connected to stress, recovery, daily routines, and mental wellness.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Scanning for problem-solution patterns and noticing how advice is structured in personal accounts.

learningObjectives: Understand the main idea of a personal article about work-related stress and recovery.
Locate specific advice on how to reduce stress and establish healthy daily limits.
Recognize and interpret common phrasal verbs related to wellbeing in context.

contextWarmup.prompt: Read this short situation: Mark stays at his desk until 9:00 PM every night and replies to emails on weekends. Lately, he feels exhausted and cannot concentrate. What is the healthiest step Mark can take first?
options: Cut back on his overtime hours and set clear limits between work and rest.
Drink more coffee during the day to keep his energy levels high.
Accept additional projects so that he forgets about his daily stress.
contextWarmup.explanation: Mark is showing early signs of exhaustion. Reducing work hours and creating clear boundaries between work and personal life helps protect mental and physical health.

rules: Rule 1: Phrasal verbs combine a base verb and a particle (like 'down', 'up', or 'with'). The particle changes the verb's normal meaning completely.
Rule 2: 'Cope with' requires an object, usually a noun or a gerund showing the difficult situation (for example: 'cope with heavy workloads').
Rule 3: Three-part phrasal verbs such as 'cut back on' cannot be separated. The object always follows the final preposition.

commonTrap.explanation: Learners often use 'cope' with an object without adding the preposition 'with'. When you name the problem or stressor, you must include 'with'.
commonTrap.wrong: He is learning to cope his stressful schedule.
commonTrap.correct: He is learning to cope with his stressful schedule.

content.passageTitle: Learning to Slow Down: Elena's Story
paragraphs: A year ago, Elena was working twelve hours a day at a busy graphic design studio in Manchester. She answered phone calls during dinner and opened client emails late at night. At first, she believed this dedication would advance her career quickly. However, after four months without a proper weekend, she began to burn out. She could not sleep well, her body felt constantly tired, and small tasks made her feel completely overwhelmed.

A visit to her family doctor became the turning point. The doctor explained that her body could no longer cope with the constant pressure. Instead of prescribing heavy medicine, he advised her to cut back on overtime and establish clear boundaries between work and home. He also urged her to reach out to her manager and discuss realistic deadlines. Elena felt nervous, but her manager was surprisingly supportive and agreed to adjust her weekly schedule.

Today, Elena's daily life looks very different. Every evening at six o'clock, she turns off her laptop and leaves her work phone in another room. To wind down, she took up evening walks in a nearby park, which helps her mind clear up after busy hours. She has also cut back on late-night caffeine. Through these simple routines, she has protected her wellbeing and rediscovered joy in her creative work.

connectedSpeech.note: The final consonant /tʃ/ blends directly into the starting vowel /ɒ/ of the particle.
The final /k/ sound of 'back' links forward into 'on', creating a single sound unit.

The affricate /tʃ/ links to /aʊ/ and 'to' reduces to a weak schwa /tə/ in fast speech.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Finding a Better Work-Life Balance

content.summary: Use clear sentences to explain what causes stress, how someone copes with it, and what helps them relax. Phrasal verbs such as burn out, wind down, switch off, and cope with can make your writing more natural. Build a paragraph with a main idea, supporting details, and a final suggestion or result.

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: Name the Cause and the Effect
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + cause of stress + and / so + effect
blueprintItems.example: Maya has too many deadlines, so she is finding it hard to cope with the pressure.

blueprintItems.title: Step 2: Describe a Healthy Routine
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + wind down / switch off + by + verb-ing
blueprintItems.example: I wind down after work by walking in the park.

blueprintItems.title: Step 3: Explain a Risk and Give Advice
blueprintItems.formula: If + subject + works too much, subject + may + burn out; subject + should + base verb
blueprintItems.example: If Leo keeps working late, he may burn out, so he should take regular breaks.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use the base form of a verb after do or does in negative sentences.
mechanicsRules.badExample: She doesn't copes well with pressure.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: She doesn't cope well with pressure.
mechanicsRules.why: The auxiliary does carries the third-person ending, so the next verb stays in its base form.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use a full stop at the end of a statement, and begin each new sentence with a capital letter.
mechanicsRules.badExample: I switch off after work i go for a walk
mechanicsRules.goodExample: I switch off after work. I go for a walk.
mechanicsRules.why: A full stop separates complete ideas and makes your writing easier to follow.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use by followed by a verb ending in -ing to explain how you do something.
mechanicsRules.badExample: He winds down by take a warm bath.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: He winds down by taking a warm bath.
mechanicsRules.why: After the preposition by, use a gerund, which is the -ing form of a verb.

content.summary: Talk about stress, healthy routines, and work-life balance. Use phrasal verbs such as cope with, wind down, and reach out in clear sentences. Give a reason or example to support your ideas.
content.audioGuidance: Speak at a steady pace and pause briefly between ideas. Make the main syllable of important words clear. Use a falling voice at the end of statements, and a rising voice for yes-or-no questions. Keep your tone calm and supportive when talking about stress.

pillars.name: Vowel Clarity
pillars.explanation: Make the vowel in stress short and clear. Hold the vowel in cope a little longer. Listen for the difference between wind, the verb, and wind, the noun.

pillars.name: Word Stress
pillars.target: Stress the main syllable in key words
pillars.explanation: Give the strongest beat to the stressed syllable in words such as overwhelm and relaxing. This helps listeners understand your meaning.

pillars.name: Phrasal Verb Rhythm
pillars.target: Say phrasal verbs as connected word groups
pillars.explanation: Keep the words in cope with and reach out close together. Make the main verb clear, then continue smoothly into the next word.

pillars.name: Intonation and Pausing
pillars.target: Use helpful pauses and natural pitch changes
pillars.explanation: Pause after a reason or before an example. Let your voice fall when you finish a statement, and rise slightly when you ask a yes-or-no question.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: Keep the main stress on cope. Say with lightly and connect it to the verb.
Stress reach more than out, and link the two words smoothly.
Give wind the stronger beat, then say down clearly but more lightly.
In cut back on, back often carries the strongest beat. Keep cut and on lighter.

reading.question: What is the main topic of the passage?
options: How a graphic designer recognized stress and restored balance in her life
The difficulties of finding a well-paid design job in Manchester
Why medical doctors prefer natural therapy over modern medicine
reading.answer: How a graphic designer recognized stress and restored balance in her life
reading.explanation: The text describes Elena's experience of working excessive hours, becoming exhausted, visiting a doctor, and successfully improving her lifestyle.

reading.question: Why did Elena initially work twelve hours a day and reply to messages at night?
options: She thought it would help her career progress quickly.
Her manager threatened to dismiss her if she refused.
She lived far away from the design studio.
reading.answer: She thought it would help her career progress quickly.
reading.explanation: Paragraph 1 states: 'At first, she believed this dedication would advance her career quickly.'

reading.question: Which symptom did Elena experience after working four months without a proper weekend?
options: She lost her voice during client meetings.
She could not sleep well and felt completely overwhelmed by small tasks.
She developed an allergy to her office environment.
reading.answer: She could not sleep well and felt completely overwhelmed by small tasks.
reading.explanation: Paragraph 1 notes that Elena could not sleep well, felt constantly tired, and found small tasks overwhelming.

reading.question: What did the family doctor identify as the source of Elena's health problems?
options: A dangerous viral infection from her workplace
Her body's inability to cope with non-stop pressure
An unhealthy diet lacking fresh fruit and vegetables
reading.answer: Her body's inability to cope with non-stop pressure
reading.explanation: Paragraph 2 states that the doctor explained her body could no longer cope with the constant pressure.

reading.question: Instead of prescribing strong medication, what did the doctor recommend?
options: Quit her job immediately and move to another city
Cut back on overtime and create boundaries between work and home
Work only on weekends so she had weekdays completely free
reading.answer: Cut back on overtime and create boundaries between work and home
reading.explanation: Paragraph 2 says the doctor advised her to cut back on overtime and establish clear boundaries between work and home.

reading.question: How did Elena's manager react when Elena spoke to him about her workload?
options: He refused to help and gave her more assignments.
He was supportive and agreed to alter her weekly schedule.
He advised her to find another design company.
reading.answer: He was supportive and agreed to alter her weekly schedule.
reading.explanation: The text states that her manager was surprisingly supportive and agreed to adjust her weekly schedule.

reading.question: What practical rule does Elena follow every evening at six o'clock?
options: She powers down her laptop and leaves her work phone in a different room.
She checks her emails one final time before cooking dinner.
She calls three new clients to prepare for the following day.
reading.answer: She powers down her laptop and leaves her work phone in a different room.
reading.explanation: Paragraph 3 explains that she turns off her laptop and leaves her work phone in another room at six o'clock.

reading.question: What new activity did Elena take up to help her wind down after work?
options: Evening walks in a nearby park
Competitive running marathons on weekends
Late-night online gaming with friends
reading.answer: Evening walks in a nearby park
reading.explanation: Paragraph 3 mentions: 'To wind down, she took up evening walks in a nearby park, which helps her mind clear up after busy hours.'

reading.question: In paragraph 2, what does the phrasal verb 'reach out' mean?
options: Communicate with someone to seek assistance or guidance
Stretch your arms physically after sitting at a desk
Apply for a promotion at another company
reading.answer: Communicate with someone to seek assistance or guidance
reading.explanation: In this context, to reach out to her manager means contacting him to talk openly about her schedule and ask for help.

reading.question: What positive outcome did Elena achieve because of these lifestyle adjustments?
options: She opened her own design agency in London.
She protected her wellbeing and found joy in her work again.
She decided to stop doing graphic design entirely.
reading.answer: She protected her wellbeing and found joy in her work again.
reading.explanation: The final sentence highlights that through these simple routines, she protected her wellbeing and rediscovered joy in her creative work.

reading.question: Identify the sentence that correctly utilizes the Third Conditional:
options: If we had anticipated the market demand, we would have expanded production sooner.
If we anticipate the market demand, we will expand production.
If we had anticipated the market demand, we will have expanded production.
If we anticipated the market demand, we would expand production sooner.
reading.answer: If we had anticipated the market demand, we would have expanded production sooner.
reading.explanation: Third conditional formula: If + past perfect, would have + past participle.

reading.question: Why did the client request an amendment to the contractual agreement?
options: To ensure delivery milestones aligned with their internal quarterly budget cycles.
Because they intended to terminate all business relations immediately.
To eliminate all warranty protections and technical support clauses.
Because the initial contract was drafted without legal counsel.
reading.answer: To ensure delivery milestones aligned with their internal quarterly budget cycles.
reading.explanation: Contract amendments in B2 business scenarios typically align scope with financial planning.

reading.question: Choose the correct passive transformation: 'The engineering team completed the audit yesterday.'
options: The audit was completed by the engineering team yesterday.
The audit had completed by the engineering team yesterday.
The engineering team was completed by the audit yesterday.
The audit is completed by the engineering team yesterday.
reading.answer: The audit was completed by the engineering team yesterday.
reading.explanation: Past simple passive: object + was/were + past participle + by agent.

reading.question: What is the primary function of the modal verb in 'You ought to back up your database before the migration'?

Logical certainty
Physical capability
Past habit
reading.explanation: 'Ought to' expresses a strong advisory recommendation or obligation.

reading.question: Which word best replaces 'alleviate' in 'measures were introduced to alleviate employee stress'?

Prolong
reading.explanation: 'Alleviate' means to make a problem or burden less severe.
